paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Isak hong tek a, kho mu thei lou khop in amit ahong mialta hi. Atapa upazaw Esau asam a, akiang ah, "Ka tapa," achi hi. Ama'n akiang ah, "Hiai ah ka om,” achi hi.
heading: Isak In Jakob Avualzawl
english: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said to him, “My son?” He said to him, “Here I am.”

paite: Ama'n, "Ngai in, ka tek mahmahta a, ka sih ni ding lah ka thei kei hi.
english: He said, “See now, I am old. I don’t know the day of my death.

paite: Tu in hehpih in na vanzat, na thaltang leh na thalpeu tawi in, va gamvak inla, sa hon va matsak in.
english: Now therefore, please take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field, and get me venison.

paite: Ka sih ma a ka hon vualzawl theihna ding in, ka duh lamtak in meh ding in limtak hon bawlsak inla, ka nek ding in ka kiang ah hon tawi in,” achi hi.
english: Make me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat, and that my soul may bless you before I die.”

paite: Isak in atapa Esau ahoupih lai Rebekah in ana za hi. Sa beng a hon po ding in Esau agamvakta hi.
english: Rebekah heard when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.

paite: Rebekah in atapa Jakob kiang ah, "Ngai in, na pa'n na u Esau kiang a athugen ka za.
english: Rebekah spoke to Jacob her son, saying, “Behold, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying,

paite: Sa hon puak inla, ka nek a ka sih ma a TOUPA ma a ka hon vualzawlna ding in, meh limtak hon bawlsak in, chi ahi.
english: ‘Bring me venison, and make me savory food, that I may eat, and bless you before Yahweh before my death.’

paite: Ka tapa, tu in ka hon thupiak bang in ka thu zui in.
english: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command you.

paite: Ganhon lak ah va hoh inla, kelnou nih hoihtak, huai a kipan hon la in. Aduh lamtak in na pa a ding in meh limtak in huai ka na bawl ding.
english: Go now to the flock and get me two good young goats from there. I will make them savory food for your father, such as he loves.

paite: Asih ma a hon vualzawlsak ding in, anek ding in na pa kiang ah na va paipih ding ahi,” achi hi.
english: You shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”

paite: Jakob in anu Rebekah kiang ah, "Ngai in, ka u Esau mimulhau ahi a, kei lah minel ka hi.
english: Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.

paite: Ka pa'n hon na zawt vialvial kha ding a, amah a ding in khempa ka hong hi dia, vualzawl gen tak louh hamsiat kizon lel ka hi kei ding maw," achi hi.
english: What if my father touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bring a curse on myself, and not a blessing.”

paite: Anu'n akiang ah, "Ka tapa, ka tung ah na hamsiat muh ding tung hen. Ka thu zui inla, hon va lak in," achi hi.
english: His mother said to him, “Let your curse be on me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go get them for me.”

paite: Huchi in akuan a, ava la a, anu kiang ah apaipihta hi. Anu'n apa duh lamtak in meh limtak abawl hi.
english: He went, and got them, and brought them to his mother. His mother made savory food, such as his father loved.

paite: Rebekah in atapa upapen Esau puansilh hoihtak, akiang a inn a om ala a, atapa naupangzaw Jakob asilhsak hi.
english: Rebekah took the good clothes of Esau, her elder son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob, her younger son.

paite: Huai ban ah kelnou vun leng akhut leh angawng nelna munte ah aphah hi.
english: She put the skins of the young goats on his hands, and on the smooth of his neck.

paite: Meh limtak leh tanghou abawlte atapa Jakob khut ah apia hi.
english: She gave the savory food and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.

paite: Amah apa kiang ah ava pai a, "Pa aw," achi a; ama'n, “Hiai ah ka om, ka tapa, akua zaw pen na hia?" achi hi.
english: He came to his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”

paite: Jakob in apa kiang ah, "Na tapa upazaw Esau ka hi; na hon sawl bang in ka hih khinta. Hehpih in thou inla, hon vualzawl ding in tu inla, ka samatsa ne in," achi hi.
english: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn. I have done what you asked me to do. Please arise, sit and eat of my venison, that your soul may bless me.”

paite: Isak in atapa kiang ah, "Ka tapa, bangchidan ahia, hong man baih na tel chia?" achi a. Ama'n, “TOUPA na Pathian in ahon lohchinsak ziak ahi," achi hi.
english: Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” He said, “Because Yahweh your God gave me success.”

paite: Isak in Jakob kiang ah, “Ka tapa, hehpih in hong pai nai dih, ka hon zawt vialvial ding, ka tapa Esau na hi na hiam," achi hi.
english: Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come near, that I may feel you, my son, whether you are really my son Esau or not.”

paite: Jakob in apa Isak ava naih a; ama'n ana zawt vialvial a, "A-aw Jakob aw hiven, akhutte lah Esau khutte hiven," achi hi.
english: Jacob went near to Isaac his father. He felt him, and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”

paite: A-u Esau khut abang a, akhut amul ziak in amah atheitel kei hi. Huchi in amah avualzawlta hi.
english: He didn’t recognize him, because his hands were hairy, like his brother Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.

paite: "Ka tapa Esau ngei na hi maw?" achi a; ama'n, "Hi e," achi hi.
english: He said, “Are you really my son Esau?” He said, “I am.”

paite: Ama'n, "Hon tawi nai in, ka hon vualzawlna ding in ka tapa samatsa ka ne ding," achi hi. Ahon tawi nai a, aneta a, uain leng ahon la a, huai leng adawn hi.
english: He said, “Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless you.” He brought it near to him, and he ate. He brought him wine, and he drank.

paite: Apa Isak in akiang ah, "Ka tapa hong pai nai in, hon tawp in," achi hi.
english: His father Isaac said to him, “Come near now, and kiss me, my son.”

paite: Ava naih a, atawp a, ama'n apuansilh gim aza a, avuałzawl hi. "En in, ka tapa gim TOUPA vualzawl gam gim bang ahi.
english: He came near, and kissed him. He smelled the smell of his clothing, and blessed him, and said, “Behold, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which Yahweh has blessed.

paite: Pathian in van daitui, lei hoihna, buh tampi leh uain tampi hon pia hen.
english: God give you of the dew of the sky, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine.

paite: Namte'n na nna sem uhenla, na ma ah namte kun uhen. Na unaute tung ah toupa in om inla; na nu tapate na ma ah kun uhen. Hon hamsiatte hamsiat in om uhenla, hon vualzawl peuhmah vualzawl in om hen," achi hi.
english: Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers. Let your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you. Blessed be everyone who blesses you.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Isak in Jakob avualzawl zohtak in, apa Isak kiang a kipan Jakob a pawtkhe man lel chih in a-unaupa, Esau sabeng ahong tung hi.
heading: Esau In Isak Vualzawlna Angen
english: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had just gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

paite: Ama'n leng meh limtak abawl a, apa kiang ah, "Ka pa aw, hong thoukhia inla, na hon vualzawl theihna ding in na tapa samatsa neta in le," achi hi.
english: He also made savory food, and brought it to his father. He said to his father, “Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that your soul may bless me.”

paite: Apa Isak in akiang ah, "Kua na hia?" achi a; ama'n, "Na tapa, na tapa upazaw, Esau ka hi," achi hi.
english: Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He said, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”

paite: Isak nakpi in aling zungzung a, "Sa va man a, ka kiang a, asa hon tawi, na hong tun ma a, ka na nek khit a, ka vualzawlpa kua ahia? Ahi, amah vualzawl in a-om ding,” achi hi.
english: Isaac trembled violently, and said, “Who, then, is he who has taken venison, and brought it to me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, he will be blessed.”

paite: Esau in apa thugen azak in nakpitak leh khase mahmah in akapta a, apa kiang ah, “Pa aw, hon vualzawl in, kei leng hon vualzawl mahmah ve aw," achi hi.
english: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me, even me also, my father.”

paite: Ama'n, “Na nau in ahong khem a, na vualzawlnate ahong laksakta," achi hi.
english: He said, “Your brother came with deceit, and has taken away your blessing.”

paite: Ama'n, “Amin Jakob achih uh dik mahmah hilou hia? Nihvei ahon suanta; ka ta masa hihna ahon laksak a; ngai in, tu in ka vualzawlna ahon laksak nawnta,” achi hi. Amah mah in, "Kei a dia vualzawlna hon sitsak lou maw?" achi hi.
english: He said, “Isn’t he rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my blessing.” He said, “Haven’t you reserved a blessing for me?”

paite: Isak in adawng a, Esau kiang ah, "Ngai in, amah na toupa in ka bawlta, a-unau tengteng leng asikha ding in akiang ah ka pe vekta, buh leh uain in leng ka vakta hi. Nang a ding in, ka tapa, bang hon hihsak ding ka hia?" achi hi.
english: Isaac answered Esau, “Behold, I have made him your lord, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants. I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then will I do for you, my son?”

paite: Esau in apa kiang ah, "Pa aw, vualzawlna khat kia ahi maw na neih? Pa aw, kei leng hon vualzawl mahmah ve," chi in ngaihtak in akapta hi.
english: Esau said to his father, “Do you have just one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.

paite: Huan apa Isak in adawng a, akiang ah, "Ngai in, na tenna ding lei hoihna tak, tunglam a kipan van daitui kiakna mun ahi ding.
english: Isaac his father answered him, “Behold, your dwelling will be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the sky from above.

paite: Na namsau in ahi na hin ding, himahleh na nau nna na sem ding hi. Hichi ahong hi ding a, na kitutkhiak hun chiang in na ngawng a kipan ahakkol na singkheta ding," achi hi.
english: You will live by your sword, and you will serve your brother. It will happen, when you will break loose, that you will shake his yoke from off your neck.”

paite: Apa'n Jakob avualzawl ziak in Esau in amudah hi. Esau in alungsim in, "Ka pa suun ni ding anaita a, huai khit chiang in ka nau Jakob ka that mai ding,” achi hi.
english: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father blessed him. Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand. Then I will kill my brother Jacob.”

paite: Atapa upazaw Esau thugen Rebekah ahilh ua; ama'n mi asawl a, atapa naupangzaw Jakob asam a, akiang ah, "Ngai in, na u Esau in na tungthu ah, nang hon thah tum in akikhamuan hi.
english: The words of Esau, her elder son, were told to Rebekah. She sent and called Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, “Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself about you by planning to kill you.

paite: Huaiziak in ka tapa, tu in ka thu mang in. Thou inla, Haran a ka sanggampa Laban kiang ah va tai in.
english: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice. Arise, flee to Laban, my brother, in Haran.

paite: Na u hehna adaih mateng akiang ah ni bangzah hiam va om tadih in;
english: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury turns away—

paite: na u hehna na tung a adaih a, atung a na thilhih amangngilh mateng. Huai chiang mi ka hon sawl ding a, huai a kipan ka hong pikhesak ding. Bangziak a ni khat thu a na nih ua hon chan tel gaode ding ka hia?" achi hi.
english: until your brother’s anger turns away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send, and get you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?”

paite: Rebekah in Isak kiang ah, "Heth tanute ziak in hin ka chimtak mahmah. Jakob in hiai gam nungak, hiai Heth tanute lak a mi zi ding a aneih nawn ngial in zaw, kei a ding in hin bang phatuam ding ahia?" achi hi.
heading: Isak In Laban Kiang Ah Jakob Asawl
english: Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, what good will my life do me?”
